must_contain.fact: A topic is a single time series of one ontology model: one topic, one model
A sequence groups the topics of one recording session, a time-bounded collection of related streams
So no: IMU and GPS are two topics of the same sequence

wrong_claims: a topic can hold several ontology models or sensor types
a sequence is a single sensor stream

must_contain.fact: Versions make queries ambiguous (which version to search?)
A session is an immutable data layer inside a sequence, the topics uploaded together as one unit
A stored sequence is extended by committing a new session with new topics; existing data is not modified
In the SDK this is SequenceUpdater, obtained from client.sequence_update() or SequenceHandler.update(); it adds new topics only

wrong_claims: a session overwrites or edits the existing topics
SequenceUpdater can change the sequence metadata or existing topics
the sequence must be re-ingested to add a topic

must_contain.fact: mosaicod is the Mosaico daemon, written in Rust, handling ingestion, retrieval and query
It speaks Apache Arrow Flight (over gRPC)
Metadata and system state live in a database (RDBMS); bulk data in an object store: S3, MinIO or the local filesystem
If the database is destroyed the data is not lost: mosaicod rebuilds the catalog by rescanning the object store

wrong_claims: the sensor data is stored in the database
losing the database loses the data
mosaicod exposes a REST/JSON API

must_contain.fact: Knowing what the data is lets Mosaico apply type-specific processing, compression, indexing and storage layout
Ontology classes are validatable (Pydantic), serializable (PyArrow) and queryable (.Q)
Data with no Python class can use Unmodeled, an ontology built at runtime from an Arrow schema; or a custom ontology class can be written

wrong_claims: Mosaico stores untyped data as opaque bytes
data without a Python class cannot be ingested

must_contain.fact: Handlers (SequenceHandler, TopicHandler) fetch metadata only and never download sensor records
Streamers deliver the data: SequenceDataStreamer merges several topics in timestamp order, TopicDataStreamer reads one topic
Both streamers accept a time window (start_timestamp_ns, end_timestamp_ns)

wrong_claims: a handler downloads the topic data
a streamer loads the whole sequence into memory

must_contain.fact: Three filter domains: sequence (name, creation time, metadata), topic (name, ontology tag, metadata), ontology (recorded values)
SDK builders QuerySequence, QueryTopic, QueryOntologyCatalog
Builders passed to one query() call are combined with a logical AND

wrong_claims: filters are combined with OR
queries are written in SQL or another query language

must_contain.fact: No: API keys are coarse-grained and grant an operation type across the whole platform, not per sequence or topic
No: read, write and delete are independent; combine them explicitly, e.g. read|write

wrong_claims: an API key can be restricted to one sequence
write includes read
TLS and API keys are the same mechanism

must_contain.fact: DataFrameExtractor flattens nested ontology fields into columns named {topic}.{ontology_tag}.{field_path}
Its output is sparse: the union of all timestamps with NaN where a sensor has no reading
SyncTransformer resamples the streams onto a fixed-frequency grid
SyncTransformer is stateful: create it once, outside the chunk loop

wrong_claims: the data must be exported to files and aligned by hand
create a new SyncTransformer for every chunk

must_contain.fact: ROS 2 bags in .mcap (and .db3, ROS 1 .bag) go through the ROS bridge (RosbagInjector)
The MCAP bridge (MCAPInjector) handles protobuf-encoded channels
MCAP channels with no adapter become Unmodeled ontologies built from the embedded schema

wrong_claims: ROS 2 .mcap bags go through the MCAP bridge
the MCAP bridge needs a message definition or generated code for every channel

must_contain.fact: The Watchdog, installed with the SDK as mosaicolabs.watchdog, ingests every new .mcap/.bag/.db3 in a folder
Daemon mode keeps watching the folder; single-pass (default) scans once and exits
One sequence per file; files already loaded are never ingested twice (state files in the folder)
Files modified in the last 30 seconds are skipped until a later scan (--min-file-age)

wrong_claims: the parts of a split recording are merged into one sequence
the Watchdog re-ingests every file on each scan
